summary: Contestants demonstrate their skills in Python programming by completing tasks that test their knowledge of structured designs, algorithms, object-oriented programming, and file I/O. The event includes an application test and, at the national level, a certification exam. All work is completed on-site and uploaded electronically.
time_limits: No more than ten (10) minutes orientation
No more than ninety (90) minutes testing time
No more than ten (10) minutes wrap-up
No more than fifty (50) minutes for certification test
submission_requirements: All student-produced jobs completed on-site are uploaded electronically and are not printed at the national level
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
Computer or laptop/notebook (USB-Type A or adapter required)
A full-size keyboard may be used (no printer is needed)
Contestant must use one of these IDEs: IDLE, Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, PyCharm, VSCode
Only pre-written code that is hard copied is allowed
competencies: Demonstrate proficiency in Python programming and apply algorithmic thinking, language syntax, core concepts, and modern practices to implement effective Python solutions
Develop modular, maintainable programs using foundational object-oriented principles in Python
Use Python file I/O to read, write, and manage data in applications
Apply structured and object-oriented design techniques and implement effective error-handling strategies to create scalable, maintainable, and resilient Python applications
Create and interpret UML diagrams to model software architecture and communicate design decisions in Python projects
Utilize Python’s built-in collections and data structures —including lists, sets, dictionaries, tuples, iterators, or related utilities—to efficiently store, manage, and manipulate data
Apply standard Python libraries and modern language features to write clean, readable, and maintainable code
judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestant within the time allotted
Business Professionals of America assumes no responsibility for hardware/software provided by the contestant
No equipment, supplies or materials other than those specified for the event will be allowed in the testing area
Previous Business Professionals of America tests and/or sample tests (handwritten, photocopied or keyed) may not be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification
Reference materials are not allowed for certification testing
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this application event
